Research profile

Mathematical foundations.
Practical AI systems.

AI researcher specializing in distributed learning, non-IID optimization, knowledge distillation, evidential uncertainty, representation learning, and applied computer vision. Primary author of the LG-FedDistill manuscript and former AI Research Intern at MNNIT Allahabad. Current independent research investigates whether uncertainty can be coupled directly to class-conditional geometry as a differentiable training objective, with ongoing work on Dirichlet evidence, hyperspherical representations, prototype learning, differentiable SVD masking, and matrix-calculus-based optimization.

RESEARCH EXPERIENCE

Research internship and current independent work
Jun 2025 – Jul 2025
Prayagraj, India

AI Research Intern | Motilal Nehru National Institute of Technology (MNNIT) Allahabad

Motilal Nehru National Institute of Technology (MNNIT) Allahabad
  • Research topic: Semi-Supervised Learning Using Knowledge Distillation via Dual Head Optimization; supervised by Dr. Joohi Chauhan.
  • Designed Dual Head Optimization (DHO) using ViT-B/16 as teacher and ResNet-34/50 as student models to separate supervised and distillation learning signals.
  • Evaluated 1%, 10%, and 20% labeled-data regimes; compared SHO/DHO, supervised vs. semi-supervised training, and raw vs. Macenko-stain-normalized inputs.
  • Achieved up to 99.45% test accuracy on Caltech101, 98.86% on Binary Cancer Detection, and 99.02% on Cervical Cancer experiments; BRACS performance improved from 14% validation accuracy on the original split to 75% after redistribution.
  • Diagnosed BRACS overfitting as strongly influenced by split structure and intra-class variation; a controlled re-split of the original training data reached 77.04% validation and 78% test accuracy.
  • Compared ViT-B/16, EfficientNet-B0, and ViT-Tiny teachers with ResNet-34/50 students; investigated the limitations and feature-loss effects of Macenko normalization.
Current
Independent research

Independent Research — Geometrical Uncertainty & Representation Learning | Independent Research

  • Formulating an uncertainty-aware representation learning framework coupling class-conditional geometry with differentiable uncertainty estimation rather than treating risk prediction as a separate auxiliary module.
  • Current formulation explores cosine similarity to EMA class prototypes, Dirichlet evidence, vacuity, predictive/Shannon entropy, and uncertainty-aware representation optimization.
  • Developed matrix-gradient derivations for the proposed uncertainty function, including gradients through cosine similarity, Dirichlet evidence, total evidence, vacuity, and entropy terms.
  • Investigating a differentiable SVD masking layer with learnable singular-value masks and nuclear-norm regularization for reducing domain-specific variation such as H&E stain shifts.
  • Research is being evaluated through explicit claims on geometry→uncertainty, evidence→geometry, uncertainty→representation, calibration/OOD behavior, and robustness to class-imbalance evidence.

PUBLICATIONS & MANUSCRIPTS

Local-Global Codistillation Framework Federated Learning (LG-FedDistill) | First Author

Manuscript With Editor — Initial Evaluation
Authors: Arpan Daniel Frank, Udbhav Agarwal, Param Patel, Chinmayee Chaini, Jackulin Mahariba A.
  • Proposed reliability-aware logit exchange and exponential validation-weighted aggregation for federated learning under controlled non-IID class skew.
  • Composite objective: L = (1−α)LCE + αLKL, with static and validation-driven dynamic α adaptation.
  • Evaluated 0%, 20%, 40%, and 60% skew across LeNet-5, EfficientNet, MiniVGG, and MobileNet; used 4 clients and 50 communication rounds.
  • At 60% skew, dynamic LG-FedDistill retained 89.63% best minority-class validation accuracy versus 48.30% for Federated Distillation, 51.60% for Federated Personalization, and 60.30% for FAMP.
  • Under 40% skew, exponential aggregation improved minority-class accuracy from 73.2% with uniform aggregation to 89.8%; dynamic α was evaluated as the proposed adaptive variant.
  • Submitted to The Journal of Supercomputing (Springer Nature). The latest status should be verified against the current submission portal.
Editorial correspondence: Springer Nature Journals Editorial Office email dated 3 August 2026 stated that the manuscript was with the editor for initial evaluation and that the editor had been contacted to expedite the process.

SELECTED APPLIED AI PROJECTS

Host-Based Intrusion Detection System (HIDS) using CNN-LSTM & Reinforcement Learning

SRM Institute of Science and Technology · Feb 2025 – Apr 2025
  • Built a modular HIDS using parallel CICIDS2017 and UNSW-NB15 pipelines with dataset-specific preprocessing, CNN-LSTM classification, and centralized Actor-Critic decision fusion.
  • Engineered a 25-feature CNN-LSTM representation; CICIDS states combine 25 input features with 15 class probabilities to form a 40-dimensional RL state.
  • Implemented four response actions: Allow Traffic, Block Traffic, Limit Bandwidth, and Raise Alert, with severity-aware multi-model fusion.
  • Designed reward shaping that penalizes incorrect actions, with heavier penalties for allowing malicious traffic; integrated real-time response concepts such as iptables blocking and tc bandwidth throttling.
  • Reported >97.8% average detection accuracy on CICIDS2017 in the paper's experiments; evaluated precision, recall, F1, and accuracy across CICIDS2017 and UNSW-NB15.
View HIDS manuscript on ResearchGate

Smart IoT-Based AI-Driven Integrated Farming

SRM Urban Farm — In-house Project · Apr 2023 – Jan 2025
  • Developed an intelligent aquaponics/hydroponics/aeroponics monitoring and control system integrating pH, TDS, temperature, humidity, and CO₂ sensing with Arduino-based edge processing.
  • Implemented local threshold-based actuation for pumps, heaters, ventilation, and an automatic fish-feeding mechanism, reducing reliance on external cloud processing.
  • Built real-time serial-data visualization using Python, Matplotlib, Tkinter, and modular navigation for aeroponics, aquaponics, hydroponics, and control-plant subsystems.
  • Integrated Arduino, ESP32/Raspberry Pi-class edge components and sensor pipelines; project documentation covers calibration, circuit design, testing, GUI, firmware, and web-server integration.
  • The earlier résumé reports a CNN leaf-disease classifier at 92% accuracy and ~30% water-use reduction; retain these figures only when presenting the corresponding experimental evidence/source.

Hybrid CNN-LSTM Model for MRI Brain Image Restoration

AI for Healthcare Project · Feb 2025 – Apr 2025
  • Designed a hybrid Conv2D-LSTM model combining spatial feature extraction with sequential consistency across MRI image slices.
  • Applied intensity normalization and CNN-based denoising; trained with Adam (learning rate 0.0001), batch size 32, for 500 epochs.
